To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the principals and senior managers of FE colleges have been socialized to the values and norms of a corporate culture that has been imposed on the sector by government policy and the market.

(a) the principal's role in the FE sector is changing in response to a new managerialism; (b) the new managerialism is based on a discourse of 'leadership'; (c) the discourse of leadership is based on a 'business model' of education; (d) the business model is a discourse which is not only managerial but which has a 'charismatic' element; and (e) the charismatic discourse has a gendered dimension which is not necessarily 'femin

principals and senior managers in FE have to be able to: 1. manage and lead others to perform well in the face of a changing policy environment; 2. manage and lead themselves to perform well in a changing policy environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the changing conditions of leadership in the FE sector and with the way in which principals and senior managers make sense of the shifting demands and expectations of the new corporate education culture.

the way in which the discourse of corporate leadership has been used to reconfigure the culture of FE and the implications this may hold for the way in which FE leaders manage and socialize their staff.
the changing nature of leadership in FE as it is experienced in the day to day management of colleges and the implications of this for staff and students.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FE sector is a complex and dynamic site for the development and implementation of leadership and management.
the FE sector has undergone a radical shift in the last decade and the role of principals and senior managers has changed significantly.
the FE sector is undergoing a period of significant change, and that these changes are having a profound effect upon the way principals and senior managers understand their own leadership role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are currently witnessing a period of change in the way in which FE is governed and managed, and that the leadership and management of FE is being increasingly defined in terms of a corporate culture.
the principals and senior managers we interviewed were able to draw on a range of personal and professional resources to manage the tensions between the competing demands of their role.
the sector is now in a state of flux and that the discourse of leadership and management is being used to legitimate and justify the changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FE sector is a case in point for the ways in which corporate leadership is being used to transform education cultures and practices.
the 'leadership' discourse is a powerful one that has become increasingly pervasive in the FE sector, as it has in other sectors.
the discourse of corporate leadership is being used in a way that is both highly selective and highly strategic.
